tasks.short: Gather the patient's screening results, labs and medication, decide the anesthesia plan, write it in the record, and discuss it with the anesthesiologist.

steps.what: Nurse anesthetist gathers screening results, labs, medication and earlier anesthesia from the record
Nurse anesthetist develops the anesthesia care plan
Nurse anesthetist writes the plan in the record
Nurse anesthetist discusses the plan with the anesthesiologist

tasks.design: A pre-operative summary view in the record ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows screening results, labs, allergies, medication and earlier anesthesia on one screen by fixed rules, so the nurse anesthetist does not gather them from several tabs. Plan templates per procedure type fill standard drugs, airway and monitoring choices that the nurse anesthetist changes as needed. Deciding the plan and agreeing it with the anesthesiologist stay with the nurse anesthetist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patient data sat in several parts of the record and plans were typed per patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Records show summary views and plan templates per procedure.
tasks.still_hard: Outside records from other hospitals are not in the view.
tasks.human_edge: Adjusting the plan for a frail patient who is anxious.

evidence.claim: Hospital records can show pre-operative summary views and plan templates per procedure.
The medical record is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient scheduled to the plan agreed; giving anesthesia is outside.
Input contract: screening and labs in the record; fallback is searching tabs.
Planning decisions stay with the nurse anesthetist and anesthesiologist.
research_questions: Are missing labs found before the day of surgery?

incremental.description: Nurse anesthetist reports outdated plan templates.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex patients with outside records; high: routine day surgery.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hand out the anesthesia leaflet, explain anesthesia, risks and alternatives, answer the patient's questions, and record consent.

steps.what: Nurse anesthetist hands out the printed anesthesia information leaflet
Nurse anesthetist explains anesthesia, risks and alternatives to obtain informed consent
Nurse anesthetist answers the patient's questions
Nurse anesthetist records consent on the paper form and in the record

tasks.design: The patient portal sends the anesthesia leaflet and a short video before the visit ({OTHER}), so the leaflet is not handed out and the patient arrives with questions. The consent form in the record ({OPS_SYSTEM}) is prefilled with patient, procedure and anesthesia type and signed on a tablet, so it is not written on paper and copied into the record. Explaining and answering questions stay with the nurse anesthetist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets were handed out at the visit and consent written on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient portals send information; records take tablet signatures.
tasks.still_hard: Patients with low literacy need everything explained in person.
tasks.human_edge: Making sure the patient has really understood the risks.

reach.learn: Whether information before the visit helps.

evidence.claim: Patient portals can send information before a visit and records can take tablet signatures.
Treatment needs the patient's informed consent under national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the consent visit to consent recorded; the surgeon's consent talk is outside.
Input contract: patient uses the portal; fallback is the printed leaflet.
Patients read the leaflet at home.
research_questions: Do patients arrive with better questions?

incremental.description: Nurse anesthetist checks whether the patient read the information.
Patients read the leaflet and watch the video in the portal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older patients who do not use the portal; high: day surgery patients who do.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take the patient through the health questionnaire, interview and examine the patient, decide fitness for anesthesia, and document the screening.

steps.what: Nurse anesthetist goes through the health questionnaire with the patient
Nurse anesthetist performs the pre-anesthetic physical evaluation and patient interview
Nurse anesthetist decides the patient's fitness for anesthesia
Nurse anesthetist documents the screening results in the record

loop.input: The screening conversation, recorded with the patient's consent, and the questionnaire answers.
loop.output: A draft screening note in the record's fields.
loop.check: Code flags any finding, medication or allergy not found in the transcript or questionnaire; the nurse anesthetist edits and validates every note before it is saved.
loop.stop: One draft per screening; if rejected, the nurse anesthetist writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questionnaire fields hold the answers, not the interview and exam findings.

tasks.design: Patients fill the health questionnaire in the patient portal at home ({OTHER}) and the answers arrive in the record, so the nurse anesthetist only goes through flagged answers instead of every question. A scribe drafts the screening note from the conversation recorded with consent; findings not in the transcript or questionnaire are flagged, and the nurse anesthetist validates every note before it is saved. Examining the patient and deciding fitness stay with the nurse anesthetist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questionnaires were gone through question by question and notes typed after the visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Portal questionnaires and scribes that draft notes for validation.
tasks.still_hard: Scribe drafts can contain errors that look plausible.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a difficult airway during the exam.
tasks.altitude: The nurse anesthetist examines and validates instead of typing.

reach.learn: Whether the questionnaire at home is easy.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation, the clinician validates the note, and it goes into the hospital record.
Providers are legally responsible for careful use of generative AI: risk assessment, training, testing and monitoring.

assumptions: Boundary: from the screening visit to the screening documented; surgery planning is outside.
Input contract: patient consents to recording; fallback is typing the note.
The nurse anesthetist validates every note.
Patients fill the questionnaire at home.
research_questions: How long does validating a drafted note take?

already_counted.description: Nurse anesthetist edits and validates drafted notes.

incremental.description: Nurse anesthetist asks patients' consent to record.
Patients fill the questionnaire in the portal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older patients who fill nothing at home; high: day surgery patients who do.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess the patient in recovery, decide corrective action or consultation, chart vital signs and scores, call the anesthesiologist for complications, and write the recovery note.

steps.what: Nurse anesthetist evaluates the patient's post-anesthesia responses
Nurse anesthetist takes corrective action or decides to request consultation
Nurse anesthetist charts vital signs and recovery scores
Nurse anesthetist phones the anesthesiologist about complications
Nurse anesthetist writes the recovery note and discharge from recovery

tasks.design: Recovery monitors send vital signs to the record ({OPS_SYSTEM}) every few minutes, and the nurse anesthetist confirms them instead of charting by hand. The discharge score is calculated from the charted values by fixed rules and the recovery note template fills vitals, drugs given and the score, so the nurse anesthetist adds only findings and decisions. Evaluating the patient, corrective action and calling the anesthesiologist stay with the nurse anesthetist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Vitals were charted by hand and recovery notes typed.
tasks.enabler_now: Monitors send vitals to the record; scores are calculated by rules.
tasks.still_hard: Artefacts in monitor data need correcting.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a patient who is quiet for the wrong reason.

evidence.claim: Patient monitors can send vital signs to the hospital record for confirmation.
The medical record is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient in recovery to the note written; ward care is outside.
Input contract: monitors linked to the record; fallback is hand charting.
Clinical decisions stay with the nurse anesthetist.

incremental.description: Nurse anesthetist corrects monitor artefacts in the record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unstable patients needing close attention; high: routine day surgery recoveries.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nurse anesthetist keeps planning, explaining, examining and treating patients; gathering data, handing out leaflets, typing notes and hand charting shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A nurse anesthetist with more time at the bedside.
